### 1 — Scene
A cafeteria-style tray meal: meat-topped noodles, sliced roast meat, lasagna, fruit salad, a brownie, and orange juice. I count all five dishes on the tray as this meal. The two water glasses contribute no energy.

### 2 — Vessels
The plates and shallow fruit bowl appear approximately **20 cm in diameter** each:  
Area = 3.14 × 10² = **314 cm² per vessel**. Perspective makes the rear dishes look smaller.

### 3–7 — Items, coverage, volume, weight, and energy
Coverage percentages below refer to each item’s own vessel. Sauces and visible cooking fat are included in the energy density of the prepared foods, rather than counted twice.

| Item | Vessel coverage | Area × average height = gross volume | Density | Estimated grams | kcal/100 g | kcal |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Sauced noodles with vegetables | 55% | 173 × 1.7 = 294 ml | 0.8 | 235 | 180 | 423 |
| Meat topping on noodles | 10% | 31 × 1.4 = 44 ml | 0.95 | 42 | 230 | 97 |
| Sliced roast meat, with juices | 50% | 157 × 1.0 = 157 ml | 0.95 | 149 | 240 | 358 |
| Lasagna | 30% | 94 × 1.8 = 169 ml | 0.95 | 161 | 170 | 274 |
| Mixed fruit pieces | 50% | 157 × 2.3 = 361 ml | 0.6 | 217 | 55 | 119 |
| Brownie | 11% | 35 × 2.0 = 69 ml | 0.9 | 62 | 430 | 267 |
| Orange juice | Glass approximately 6 cm across; liquid depth 8.5 cm | 28.3 × 8.5 = 240 ml | 1.04 | 250 | 45 | 113 |

**Coverage check:** The noodle plate is approximately 65% covered, roast-meat plate 50%, lasagna plate 30%, fruit bowl 50%, and brownie plate 11%. These match the substantial visible empty rims.

### 8 — Sanity check
Approximately **866 g of food**, plus **250 g of juice**, is plausible for this multi-dish tray. Estimated total: **1,116 g and 1,650 kcal**. The largest uncertainties are the depth of the meat pile and the noodles’ oil content.
